title: Ebola Outbreak Reaches 10,000 Cases as Health Officials Call for Urgent Action
subtitle: The fastest-spreading Ebola crisis in history continues to challenge medical teams across Africa.

summary.en: The Ebola outbreak has officially surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases, marking a record-breaking speed of transmission. Health authorities are struggling to contain the virus as it spreads across multiple African countries. The current crisis is complicated by a rare virus type that lacks an approved vaccine. Medical teams face significant obstacles, including regional conflict and public mistrust in health services. International leaders are now calling for better coordination to stop the disease from crossing more borders.
summary.zh: 伊波拉疫情的官方確診病例已突破一萬例，傳播速度創下歷史紀錄。隨著病毒擴散至多個非洲國家，衛生當局正努力遏制疫情。目前的危機因缺乏核准疫苗的罕見病毒株而變得更加複雜。醫療團隊面臨包括區域衝突與公眾對醫療服務不信任等重大障礙。國際領袖現正呼籲加強協調，以防止疾病跨越更多國界。

paragraphs.en: The Ebola outbreak currently affecting parts of Africa has reached a difficult new milestone, with government data confirming more than 10,000 cases since the crisis was first declared in May. This development confirms that the current situation is the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak in history. According to reports from the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ministry of Health, nearly half of those infected have died, making it the deadliest such event in the country’s history.
paragraphs.zh: 目前影響非洲部分地區的伊波拉病毒疫情已達到一個艱難的新里程碑，政府數據證實，自五月宣布危機以來，確診病例已超過一萬例。這一發展證實，目前的疫情是歷史上傳播速度最快的伊波拉疫情。根據剛果民主共和國衛生部的報告，感染者中近半數已經死亡，使其成為該國歷史上最致命的疫情事件。

paragraphs.en: Katie Thomas-Canfield, an official with the International Rescue Committee, described the speed of the spread as "staggering." While a previous outbreak in West Africa from 2014 to 2016 had a higher total number of cases, the current crisis has reached this high number in a much shorter period. The virus has now moved beyond the Democratic Republic of Congo, with cases recorded in Kenya, Nigeria, Uganda, and France, though the latter two countries currently have no active cases.
paragraphs.zh: 國際救援委員會（International Rescue Committee）的官員凱蒂·湯瑪斯-坎菲爾（Katie Thomas-Canfield）形容病毒擴散的速度「令人震驚」。雖然二零一四年至二零一六年間西非曾發生過一次病例總數更高的疫情，但目前的危機在更短的時間內就達到了如此高的病例數。該病毒目前已擴散至剛果民主共和國境外，肯亞、奈及利亞、烏干達和法國皆有病例紀錄，不過後兩國目前並無現存病例。

paragraphs.en: One of the primary reasons for the rapid spread is that the outbreak is caused by a rare type of the virus known as Bundibugyo. Because this specific type is uncommon, existing medical tests were not originally designed to detect it, which caused delays in identifying early cases. Furthermore, experts suggest that the virus likely began spreading in February or March, months before it was officially recognized. This delay meant that health responders started their work at a significant disadvantage.
paragraphs.zh: 疫情迅速擴散的主要原因之一，在於此次疫情是由一種名為「本迪布焦」（Bundibugyo）的罕見病毒株所引起。由於這種特定類型並不常見，現有的醫療檢測最初並未針對檢測該病毒而設計，導致早期病例的識別出現延誤。此外，專家認為該病毒很可能在二月或三月就已開始傳播，比官方正式確認的時間早了數月。這種延誤意味著醫療應對人員在展開工作時，處於極為不利的境地。

paragraphs.en: Medical teams on the ground are facing a very difficult environment. Many of the affected areas in northeastern Congo are remote and suffer from ongoing armed conflict. These conditions make it hard to provide care and track the movement of the disease. According to MedPage Today, responders are also dealing with poor roads and violence from local residents who are often suspicious of medical staff. This mistrust, combined with misinformation, has created a barrier that prevents many people from seeking help or reporting their symptoms.
paragraphs.zh: 在當地的醫療團隊正面臨極其困難的環境。剛果東北部許多受影響地區位置偏遠，且飽受武裝衝突之苦。這些條件使得提供照護與追蹤疾病動向變得十分困難。根據《今日醫學頁》（MedPage Today）報導，應對人員還必須應付惡劣的道路狀況，以及當地居民對醫護人員常有的猜忌與暴力行為。這種不信任感加上錯誤資訊，形成了一道阻礙，導致許多民眾不願尋求協助或通報症狀。

paragraphs.en: Another major challenge is the lack of an approved vaccine or specific treatment for this rare type of Ebola. Without these tools, health workers must rely on supportive care to help patients recover. Despite these hardships, there have been some positive moments. In a recent video from Ituri province, health workers were seen celebrating as the last two patients were discharged from a treatment center. According to the World Health Organization, more than 2,600 people have recovered from the disease so far.
paragraphs.zh: 另一個主要挑戰是缺乏針對這種罕見伊波拉病毒的核准疫苗或特定療法。在缺乏這些工具的情況下，醫護人員必須仰賴支持性療法來協助患者康復。儘管困難重重，仍有一些正面的時刻。在伊圖里省（Ituri）最近的一段影片中，可以看到醫護人員在最後兩名患者出院時歡呼慶祝。根據世界衛生組織（World Health Organization）的數據，迄今已有超過兩千六百人從該疾病中康復。

paragraphs.en: However, the overall situation remains critical. Data from the Africa CDC indicates that about 80% of new cases are coming from people who were not previously identified as contacts of known patients. For health officials to say an outbreak is under control, they generally need to identify at least 95% of new cases through contact tracing—the process of finding everyone who has been near an infected person. The current low percentage suggests that the virus is still moving through communities undetected.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，整體局勢依然危急。非洲疾病管制暨預防中心（Africa CDC）的數據顯示，約百分之八十的新增病例來自先前未被列為已知患者接觸者的民眾。衛生官員若要宣稱疫情受到控制，通常需要透過接觸者追蹤——即找出所有曾與感染者接觸過的人——來識別至少百分之九十五的新增病例。目前偏低的比例顯示，病毒仍在社區中未被察覺地持續傳播。

paragraphs.en: International support has also been a point of concern. While the United States has pledged more than $880 million, some health workers report that the money is slow to arrive. Additionally, some experts, such as infectious disease physician Nahid Bhadelia, note that fewer international healthcare workers are traveling to help compared to previous outbreaks. This is partly due to concerns about government policies regarding the return of medical staff who might become sick while working abroad. As a result, the burden of the response is falling heavily on local and regional medical teams.
paragraphs.zh: 國際支援也是令人擔憂的一點。雖然美國已承諾提供超過八點八億美元的資金，但一些醫護人員反映資金到位速度緩慢。此外，傳染病醫師娜希德·巴德利亞（Nahid Bhadelia）等專家指出，與過去的疫情相比，前往協助的國際醫護人員較少。這部分歸因於各國政府對於在海外工作可能染病的醫護人員返國後的相關政策感到擔憂。結果，應對疫情的重擔沉重地壓在當地與區域醫療團隊身上。

paragraphs.en: In response to the growing threat, African health ministers are preparing for a virtual summit to improve their collective efforts. Jean Kaseya, the head of the Africa CDC, emphasized that because the virus is crossing borders, the response must involve stronger coordination and decisive leadership. As Mohamed Janabi of the World Health Organization Africa noted, the goal is to reach people earlier and provide safe care, while also working to build trust within communities. Until these goals are met, the fight against this record-breaking outbreak remains a dangerous and uncertain road for everyone involved.
paragraphs.zh: 為了應對日益嚴峻的威脅，非洲各國衛生部長正準備召開一場視訊高峰會，以加強集體應對行動。非洲疾病管制暨預防中心負責人尚·卡塞亞（Jean Kaseya）強調，由於病毒正在跨越國界，應對措施必須包含更強的協調與果斷的領導。正如世界衛生組織非洲區的穆罕默德·賈納比（Mohamed Janabi）所言，目標是更早接觸到民眾並提供安全的照護，同時致力於建立社區內的信任。在達成這些目標之前，對抗這場破紀錄疫情的道路，對所有參與者而言依然充滿危險與不確定性。

keyTerms.noteZh: 此處指疫情發展到一個嚴重的階段，而非字面上的「里程碑」。文中：The Ebola outbreak currently affecting parts of Africa has reached a difficult new milestone, with government data confirming more than 10,000 cases since the crisis was first declared in May.

keyTerms.definitionEn: In the actual location where an event or activity is happening.
keyTerms.noteZh: 指實際在受災地區工作的醫護人員。文中：Medical teams on the ground are facing a very difficult environment.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To become the responsibility of someone.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「掉落」，此處指責任歸屬。文中：As a result, the burden of the response is falling heavily on local and regional medical teams.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason for the delay in identifying early cases of the current Ebola outbreak?

options.A: A lack of international funding for medical testing equipment.
options.B: The existing medical tests were not designed to detect the specific strain of the virus.
options.C: Health responders were unable to reach remote areas in northeastern Congo in time.
options.D: The virus was misidentified as a different, less dangerous disease by local staff.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，目前的爆發是由一種罕見的 Bundibugyo 病毒株引起，因為該類型不常見，現有的醫療檢測工具並未針對其設計，導致早期病例辨識延遲。選項 A 雖然文章後段有提到資金問題，但與早期檢測延遲無關。選項 C 是導致醫療困難的因素，而非檢測延遲的主因。選項 D 文章並未提及誤診為其他疾病。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why is the current Ebola outbreak considered particularly difficult to control?

options.A: Because the virus is now spreading rapidly through air travel across all continents.
options.B: Because the total number of deaths has already surpassed the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak.
options.C: Because the majority of new cases are appearing in people who were not previously tracked by health officials.
options.D: Because there is a complete lack of medical staff willing to work in the affected regions.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第六段提到，目前約 80% 的新病例來自未被列入追蹤名單的人，而要控制疫情通常需要透過接觸者追蹤掌握 95% 的案例，這顯示病毒仍在隱蔽傳播。選項 A 誇大了傳播範圍，僅提到部分非洲國家及法國，且未強調空運。選項 B 文章僅提到此為史上傳播速度最快，未說死亡總數已超越 2014 年。選項 D 錯誤，雖國際人員減少，但當地醫療團隊仍在運作。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'barrier' most likely mean in the context of the medical response?

options.A: A physical wall built to separate medical staff from local residents.
options.B: A difficult obstacle or challenge that prevents progress.
options.C: A medical device used to protect health workers from infection.
options.D: A legal rule that restricts the movement of people in infected areas.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在文中，作者提到「 mistrust, combined with misinformation, has created a barrier」，意指不信任感與錯誤資訊造成了阻礙，導致民眾不願求醫。這是一種抽象的障礙。選項 A 誤將其視為實體牆壁。選項 C 與 D 則完全曲解了該詞在文中的比喻用法，文中並未提及物理防護設備或法律限制。

quiz.question: Which of the following best summarizes the main message of the article?

options.A: The Ebola outbreak is finally being contained due to international financial support.
options.B: The current Ebola crisis is a complex, record-breaking challenge hampered by logistical, social, and medical obstacles.
options.C: The Democratic Republic of Congo is solely responsible for managing the current Ebola crisis.
options.D: Medical technology has successfully identified a new vaccine to stop the spread of the Bundibugyo virus.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。全文旨在探討此次 Ebola 疫情的嚴重性，並從病毒特性、地理環境、社會不信任、資源缺乏及國際支援不足等多個面向，說明為何此疫情難以控制。選項 A 與事實不符，疫情仍處於危險階段。選項 C 錯誤，文章強調需要國際合作與跨國協調。選項 D 錯誤，文章第五段明確指出目前缺乏核准的疫苗或特定治療方法。
